newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 could break 2,000 level next month.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 could break 2,000 level next month.

text.p: Brussels' Bel-20 index, at an all-time high, was expected to stay firm in Friday trade, with dealers forecasting the index would extend its record climb in coming weeks, helped by the Dow's bullish run.
The Bel-20 was at 1,862.77, up 0.4 percent, also pushed on by a steady dollar.

"We've had to do some upward revision and now feel confident the Bel-20 could climb to 1,900 or even break the psychological 2,000 barrier in the coming month," said a trader. "There's much panic buying, much private money from individuals, wanting to get in while the going is good," said another.
Traders said there were few places to put liquidities, given that interest rates were low and bond yields falling.
Pharmaceuticals and chemicals firm UCB stayed in the limelight after a strong week, trading at 78,650, up 3.49 percent or 2,650 francs.
"UCB's run is no surprise after their recent promotional world tour, with Japan likely to become an important market for UCB," said a dealer.
Insurer Fortis AG stayed firm, up 1.48 percent at 4,810 francs, reflecting confidence in the insurance sector, traders said.

Utilities holding company Tractebel held up well on the first day of trading in the put warrant, slipping 600 francs to 14,440. Good news, a trader said. The warrant was at 562 francs after a 600 franc high.
Steelmaker Cockerill slipped to 118 francs, down 1.67 percent, after a weak week. One analyst said the steady fall in the British steel sector since September 30 affected Cockerill.
